result.question: I want to know whether the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at site MAIN is heading into trouble over the next couple of days, not just whether it looks bad today. Using the co and co2 samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, first check both series for gaps and tell me how many usable samples each has. Then try at least two forecasting models on co, including a simple last-value baseline, and backtest them on the final held-out sample. Give me each model's error and pick the one with the lowest error. Only prefer a pretrained model over the baseline if its error is at least 10% lower. Use the chosen approach to forecast co and co2 two days ahead, one step per day, with an 80% prediction interval for each day. From those forecasts, work out the projected CO2/CO ratio for each day. If the projected ratio drops below 3 on either day, treat it as likely paper involvement in a fault, tell me which day, and recommend an insulation check plus a confirmatory oil sample. If it stays between 3 and 10, call it normal and say no action is needed. If it goes above 10, flag general cellulose ageing for the next routine review. If co2 has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't forecast the ratio. Forecast co alone and flag any day where its upper bound is more than 20% above the latest co reading, and say that the ratio test couldn't be done. If co itself has fewer than 4 usable samples, skip the models and report only the first-to-last change in co per day as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
I couldn't run the forecasting service on this data because there was no way to give it the samples. The TSFM tools only accept a data file, I had no tool to create one, and they rejected a direct IoT address ("Protocol not known: iot"). So no pretrained model was tested. I ran the models and intervals below by hand using standard formulas.

**1. Gaps and usable samples (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19)**

| Date | co (ppm) | co2 (ppm) |
|---|---|---|
| 01-15 | 32 | 1344 |
| 01-16 | 30 | 1300 |
| 01-17 | 35 | 1350 |
| 01-18 | 33 | 1325 |

- **co:** 4 usable samples, one per day, no gaps or missing values.
- **co2:** 4 usable samples, one per day, no gaps or missing values.

Both series have at least 4 samples, so I ran the full model comparison and ratio test.

**2. Backtest on co (fit on 01-15 to 01-17, predict the held-out 01-18 value of 33)**

| Model | Prediction | Absolute error |
|---|---|---|
| Last value (baseline) | 35.0 | 2.00 |
| Historical mean | 32.33 | **0.67** |
| Drift (trend continued) | 36.5 | 3.50 |

The historical mean has the lowest error, 67% lower than the baseline. The 10% rule only applies to pretrained models, so it doesn't affect this choice. **I chose the historical mean.** One held-out sample is very little evidence, so this choice is weak.

**3. Two-day forecast (mean of all 4 samples, 80% prediction interval using a t-distribution with 3 degrees of freedom)**

| Day | co (80% PI) | co2 (80% PI) | CO2/CO ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-19 | 32.5 (28.7 – 36.3) | 1329.8 (1288.5 – 1371.0) | **40.9** |
| 2024-01-20 | 32.5 (28.7 – 36.3) | 1329.8 (1288.5 – 1371.0) | **40.9** |

Even the most extreme combinations of the interval bounds give a ratio between about 35.5 and 47.8.

**4. Verdict**

The projected ratio never drops below 3, so nothing points to paper being involved in a fault on either day. It stays above 10 on both days, which matches the recent ratios (about 40). That points to general, gradual ageing of the paper insulation, not an emerging fault. **Flag general cellulose ageing for the next routine review.** No urgent insulation check or confirmatory oil sample is needed.

score.rationale: The agent correctly retrieved co and co2 for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window via iot.history, and its hand calculations (4 usable samples each, last-value/mean/drift backtest errors, t-based 80% intervals, projected CO2/CO ratio ≈ 40.9, verdict of general cellulose ageing for routine review) are arithmetically sound and honestly caveated. However, the required TSFM workflow was not executed: no tsfm.data_quality gap check, no tsfm.find_models shortlist, and no tsfm.run_recipe bac

details.suggestions: The agent correctly retrieved co and co2 for Transformer 1 at MAIN over the requested window via iot.history, and its hand calculations (4 usable samples each, last-value/mean/drift backtest errors, t-based 80% intervals, projected CO2/CO ratio ≈ 40.9, verdict of general cellulose ageing for routine review) are arithmetically sound and honestly caveated. However, the required TSFM workflow was not executed: no tsfm.data_quality gap check, no tsfm.find_models shortlist, and no tsfm.run_recipe backtests or forecasts. After a single failed profile_series call with an unsupported 'iot://' path, the agent abandoned the toolchain instead of trying alternatives (e.g., materializing the observations to a dataset file/path the TSFM tools accept, or checking run_recipe's accepted dataset_path formats). Consequently no pretrained catalog model was ever tested against the baseline, so the 10%-improvement rule could not be applied as specified, and the prediction intervals are manual rather than conformal/tool-derived. To rectify: persist the retrieved series in a supported format, run tsfm.data_quality on both channels, use tsfm.find_models to pick at least one catalog model, run tsfm.run_recipe backtests (catalog model + naive last-value) holding out the final sample, apply the 10% rule, then run the chosen recipe with fh=[1,2] and conformal coverage 0.8 for both co and co2 before computing the ratio.
